drivers.title: Oil jumps to a four-year high
drivers.text: Brent rose about 3% to above $116 a barrel, its highest since June 2022, on Middle East supply worries. Oil pushed the S&P 500 down 0.5% and the Dow down about 650 points.

drivers.title: AI spending doubts hit tech and bonds
drivers.text: Thursday's selloff began when Meta fell nearly 8% after earnings and a plan to issue non-voting shares to fund AI spending, and the 10-year fell to about 4.95% as buyers rushed into Treasuries. It rebounded to 5.00% Friday.

drivers.title: Fed decides Wednesday
drivers.text: Futures give about a 90% chance the Fed holds at 3.75–4.00% on 28 Oct after September's hike. Chair Warsh's guidance is the focus, as the same week brings Microsoft, Alphabet and Amazon earnings.

sowhat.text: A $14B all-stock gas merger from EQT and Range, plus CRH closing Arcosa, show strategics still doing large deals with the 10-year at 5%. Credit spreads stay tight, so financing is open, though oil and AI capex worries add volatility.

pitch: Stocks slipped on Friday. The S&P fell about half a percent and the Dow lost over 600 points, mostly because oil jumped again, with Brent above 116 dollars, the highest since 2022. Second, doubts about AI spending, which started with Meta on Thursday, pushed money into Treasuries, and the 10-year ended the week at 5%. Third, the Fed meets Wednesday and futures price about a 90% chance it holds at 3.75 to 4%. On the M&A side, deals keep coming despite high rates. This morning EQT agreed to buy Range Resources in an all-stock deal creating a gas producer worth over 50 billion dollars, and CRH closed its 8.5 billion dollar Arcosa purchase.

quiz.q: Where did the 10-year Treasury close on Friday 23 Oct?
quiz.a: 5.00%, up 4 bp after falling to 4.96% on Thursday.

quiz.q: Why did the S&P 500 and Dow fall on Friday 23 Oct?
quiz.a: Oil jumped, with Brent above $116 on Middle East supply worries.
options: Oil jumped on Middle East supply worries

quiz.q: Who advised Range Resources on its merger with EQT?
quiz.a: Evercore (lead) and J.P. Morgan, with Gibson Dunn as legal counsel; EQT used Citi and RBC.
